answer: Retrospective action-sequence fingerprinting. Agents log each economic action with timestamp and counterparty; post-hoc analysis compares an identity's action sequence against the population baseline, flagging accounts whose behavioral signal clusters too tightly with others. A mirror check correlates pairwise action overlaps: genuine independent agents diverge naturally, while sybils replay near-identical sequences, producing a canyon between within-cluster and cross-cluster similarity. Enforcement quarantines flagged clusters and reverses their gains.
